about.title: Burbank Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products rarely give warning. A space heater, an e-bike battery, a ladder, or a set of replacement tires works fine in a Burbank home or workplace until the day it doesn't, and by then someone is hurt. California handles these injuries differently from an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict liability, you generally need to show only that the product carried a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury — you don't have to prove the company was careless. The manufacturer, the distributor, and the store that sold it may each share responsibility. That framework matters for vehicles as well. Burbank logged 209 injury collisions in 2025, with 297 people hurt and no traffic deaths, with the highest counts recorded along I-5, SR-134, and Glenoaks Boulevard; a portion of collisions anywhere trace back to a failed part rather than a driver's error. Whatever the product, keep it. LawProactive is a free connection service in Los Angeles County, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys we match you with work on contingency.

whyChoose.title: How a Product Liability Attorney Approaches a Burbank Case

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California the central issue is usually whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect that caused your injury — not whether anyone was careless. An attorney frames the claim around that standard from the start.

items.title: The Product Is the Evidence
items.desc: A cracked helmet, a scorched charger, or a sheared bolt tells the story better than anyone's memory can. Your attorney can help you preserve the item, its packaging, and any receipts before they are lost or thrown away.

items.title: More Than One Party May Answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all be held responsible under California law. An attorney identifies every link in that chain rather than stopping at the company whose name is on the box.

items.question: My airbag didn't deploy in a crash on the 134 in Burbank. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. The collision itself may involve a claim against another driver, while a failed airbag, seat belt, or brake component may support a separate product liability claim against the maker or seller. Keep the vehicle from being repaired or salvaged until it has been inspected, because the part itself is the key evidence. An attorney can help you sort out which claims apply.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer did something wrong?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was negligent is usually not the deciding question.

items.question: I bought the item at a Burbank store but it was made by a company overseas. Who is responsible?
items.answer: Under California law, responsibility can extend to the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer that sold you the product. That means a local store can be part of the claim even if the maker is located far away. An attorney reviews the supply chain to determine which parties may be held accountable in your situation.
